Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

powerful adjective

also mighty, influential, a powerful man, the powerful, strong (of a person), strong

classical

Cic. Imp. Pomp. 4: duo potentissimī rēgēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. possum)
Ov. F. 4.255: Rōma potēns opibus

potēns, potentis

adjective, third declension

powerful, mighty, influential

Of people, cities and families with power or influence; with the genitive, master of (meī potēns, “my own master”, Liv. 26.13.14).

Other words

  • validus, valida, validum — strong, powerful, robust

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 1.1.7 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 5.33 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 66: strong (opposite imbēcillus)

    Strength of body or force (a strong man, a powerful remedy); mostly poetic and post-Augustan, rare in Cicero, never in Caesar, who would say valēns (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • humilēs labōrant ubi potentēs dissident

    when the powerful quarrel, the humble sufferPhaedr. 1.30.1

See also effective, strength.
